title: Spiral spins both ways
caption: The Propeller Galaxy, NGC 7479, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7479 · constellation Pegasus · about 110 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The tightly wound arms of the spiral galaxy NGC 7479 trace an inverted 'S' in this Hubble image, turning anticlockwise. Many bright young stars dot its arms and disc. The three brightest stars nearby, though, are foreground stars that simply lie between the galaxy and Hubble.

In radio light, the galaxy, sometimes called the Propeller Galaxy, seems to spin the other way. It has a jet of radiation that bends opposite to the stars and dust in its arms. Astronomers think a merger with another galaxy set the radio jet into this strange backwards twist.

Galactic collisions tend to reignite star formation, and NGC 7479 is indeed going through a starburst. Through a moderate-sized telescope it appears as an elongated fuzzy patch of light, while its spiral arms can be glimpsed, with more difficulty, in larger telescopes under dark skies.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.65 x 2.72 arcminutes) and distance (110 million light years), the frame spans roughly 85,000 × 87,000 light-years. Its light set out about 110 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines visible and near-infrared light from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Light through a yellow filter (F555W) is coloured blue and near-infrared light (F814W) is coloured red.
understand.eye: The red channel is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the colours are assigned rather than natural.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was made with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Each filter had a total exposure of 520 seconds, and the view spans 2.7 arcminutes.
alt: A spiral galaxy whose tightly wound arms form an inverted S shape, with three bright foreground stars nearby.
